Can States & Preservation Process
Understanding the full lifecycle of a can.

Cans move through several stages before food is fully preserved. Each state represents a step in preparation, sealing, and processing. Until a can is fully pressure processed, its contents remain raw and will continue to spoil.

Steel Can
────────────────────────
The Steel Can is forged at the anvil using 2 Steel Ingots. Smithing one recipe produces 8 Steel Cans. This is the structural base container and cannot safely store food in its raw state.

Empty Can
────────────────────────
Steel Cans must be treated with a protective tin coating before use. This is done by placing them in a sealed barrel containing diluted cassiterite. Each can requires 1 liter of solution and takes 24 hours to complete after sealing the barrel.

*Note: The amount of solution required per can can be adjusted in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Once finished, the can becomes an Empty Can. Empty Cans can only be used at the Canning Bench and are capable of holding raw ingredients used in base game meal preparation.

Filled Can
────────────────────────
An Empty Can filled at the Canning Bench becomes a Filled Can. The contents will display a list of the stored ingredients. At this stage, the ingredients are still raw and will continue to spoil if not processed further.

Sealed Can
────────────────────────
A Filled Can must be sealed using a lid at the Canning Press. This creates a Sealed Can. Sealing is required for preservation, but sealing alone does not preserve the contents. The ingredients inside remain raw and will continue to spoil until properly pressure processed.

Preserved Can
────────────────────────
Sealed Cans must be processed in the Pressure Cooker to complete preservation. Once pressure cooked, the can becomes a Preserved Can — the final state.

Preserved Cans greatly reduce spoilage. While base game sealed crocks extend food life by ~10x the normal spoil rate, preserved cans increase this value to 25x the normal rate — offering more than double the preservation compared to sealed crocks. This makes them ideal for extended storage, travel, and emergency supplies.

*Note: The spoilage multiplier for preserved cans is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Opened Can
────────────────────────
A Preserved Can that has been opened with a Can Opener becomes an Opened Can. There are two ways to consume the contents:

Direct eating: Select the Opened Can in your hotbar and hold Right mouse. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the can itself.

Bowl eating: Similar to taking servings out of a crock with a bowl, you can do the same with an opened can. Simply place the opened can on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out.

Once all servings have been consumed or removed, the Opened Can automatically returns to an Empty Can, ready to be refilled and reused.

Note: The 25× preservation bonus only applies while the can is sealed. Once opened, the meal returns to a normal spoilage rate and should be consumed in a timely manner.

Rotten Can
────────────────────────
Warning: Filled Cans and Sealed Cans are only partially processed. Their contents remain raw and will continue to spoil at normal rates. If either state is left too long, the contents will rot and contaminate the can, producing a Rotten Can.

Contamination permanently damages the container, rendering it unsafe for food use. Rotten Cans must be discarded or broken down into steel bits, as they can no longer be reused for preservation.

Hot Cans
────────────────────────
Preserved Cans come out of the Pressure Cooker at high temperature. Use Canning Tongs to handle them safely. See the Hot System guide for full details.

Tinning Process – Steel Cans & Lids
Preparing steel components for safe food preservation.

Before Steel Cans or Steel Lids can be used for food preservation, they must undergo a tinning process. Tinning prevents contamination and prepares the metal for long-term food contact. This process is completed by sealing the items inside a barrel filled with diluted cassiterite.

Tinning Steel Cans
────────────────────────
Each Steel Can requires 1 liter of diluted cassiterite during the sealing process. Steel Cans stack up to 16, meaning a full stack requires 16 liters of diluted cassiterite when sealed in a barrel. The barrel will process up to 16 Steel Cans at a time, provided enough solution is present.

Once sealed, the barrel must remain closed for 24 in-game hours. After processing completes, the Steel Cans are converted into Empty Cans. The number of Empty Cans produced equals the number of Steel Cans originally placed into the barrel.

*Note: The amount of diluted cassiterite required per Steel Can is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Tinning Steel Lids
────────────────────────
Each Steel Lid requires 0.1 liters of diluted cassiterite during the sealing process. Steel Lids stack up to 32, meaning a full stack requires 3.2 liters of diluted cassiterite when sealed in a barrel. The barrel will process up to 32 Steel Lids at a time, provided enough solution is present.

Once sealed, the barrel must remain closed for 24 in-game hours. After processing completes, the Steel Lids are converted into Canning Lids. The number of Canning Lids produced equals the number of Steel Lids originally placed into the barrel.

*Note: The amount of diluted cassiterite required per Steel Lid is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Canning Bench
Used to fill Empty Cans and Glass Jars with prepared meal ingredients.

The Canning Bench is the first active stage of the canning process for both Metal Cans and Glass Jars. It is used to combine an Empty Can or Glass Jar with raw ingredients that match valid base game meal recipes.

Slot Layout
────────────────────────
The bench contains 5 input slots and 1 output slot.

Container Slot: Accepts either an Empty Can or an Empty Glass Jar. No other items may be placed in this slot.
Ingredient Slots (4): Accept raw ingredients that correspond to valid base game meal combinations.
Output Slot: Produces the Filled Can or Filled Jar once processing is complete.

Ingredient Requirements
────────────────────────
The Canning Bench follows the same ingredient rules as base game meal preparation. Ingredients must match a valid meal type and proper ratios. The interface will display a text notification at the top of the GUI indicating whether the ingredient ratios are correct and if they match an existing vanilla meal.

For valid ingredient combinations and ratios, refer to Cooking Recipes in the base game handbook.

Jam Meals
────────────────────────
Jam meals can only be filled into Glass Jars. They cannot be used with Empty Cans. If you are looking to preserve a jam meal, make sure a Glass Jar is placed in the container slot.

Filling the Container
────────────────────────
Once valid ingredients and at least one Empty Can or Glass Jar are present, hold right-click on the Canning Bench to begin filling. A progress bar will appear. After approximately 4 seconds, the process completes and a Filled Can or Filled Jar is produced in the output slot.

If ingredient ratios are incorrect, the bench will not produce a result. Ensure the recipe matches a valid base game meal before attempting to fill.

Glass Jar States & Preservation Process
Understanding the full lifecycle of a glass jar.

Glass Jars move through several stages before food is fully preserved. Each state represents a step in preparation, sealing, and processing. Until a jar is fully processed in the Canning Pot, its contents remain raw and will continue to spoil.

Crafting Glass Jars
────────────────────────
Two base jar types can be crafted directly. Placing a Hammer, Chisel, and either a Plain Glass Block or a Quartz Glass Block in the crafting grid will yield 4 Glass Jars of the corresponding type.

*Note: The number of jars produced per craft is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may adjust this value to better fit their world balance.

Jar Variants
────────────────────────
Glass Jars come in 12 color variants. Beyond the two base types, the remaining 10 can be created through barrel processing:

Dyed variants (7): Place a Plain Glass Jar in a sealed barrel with 2 liters of the desired dye color. After 48 hours the jar will take on that color. This covers Red, Green, Blue, Violet, Orange, Pink, and Yellow.

Vintage: Place a Plain Glass Jar in a sealed barrel with 2 liters of diluted cassiterite. After 48 hours it becomes a Vintage Glass Jar.

Smoky: Place a Quartz Glass Jar in a sealed barrel with 2 liters of Gray Dye. After 48 hours it becomes a Smoky Glass Jar.

Brown: Place a Plain Glass Jar in a sealed barrel with 2 liters of Weak Tannin. After 48 hours it becomes a Brown Glass Jar.

All variants function identically and differ only in appearance.

Lid Types & Preservation Tiers
────────────────────────
How well a Glass Jar preserves food depends on which lid is used to seal it.

Wooden Lid (~10x): Provides approximately 10x the normal spoil rate — on par with a vanilla sealed crock.

Wooden Lid with Beeswax (~12x): Adding beeswax as a secondary seal bumps preservation up to approximately 12x. To apply beeswax, the jar must already have a Wooden Lid applied. Hold beeswax in your active hotbar slot and right-click the jar.

Metal Lid (~15x): Brings preservation to approximately 15x the normal spoil rate, though still below what Preserved Cans offer.

*Note: All preservation multiplier values are configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may adjust these values to better fit their world balance.

Filled Jar
────────────────────────
An Empty Jar filled at the Canning Bench becomes a Filled Jar. The contents will display a list of the stored ingredients. At this stage the ingredients are still raw and will continue to spoil if not processed further.

Applying & Removing Lids
────────────────────────
Lids are applied directly to jars placed in the world rather than through the Canning Press. Place the jar on the ground, then with the desired lid selected in your active hotbar slot, hold Shift and Right mouse to seal it. If you change your mind, the lid can be removed the same way with an empty hotbar slot. Once sealed, right-click the jar to pick it up.

Applying Beeswax: A Wooden Lid can be upgraded with a beeswax seal to increase preservation from ~10x up to ~12x. With beeswax held in your active hotbar slot, right-click the jar.

Sealed Jar
────────────────────────
A Filled Jar with a lid applied becomes a Sealed Jar. Sealing is required before the jar can be processed, but the lid alone does not preserve the contents. The ingredients inside remain raw and will continue to spoil until the jar has been through the Canning Pot.

Preserved Jar
────────────────────────
Sealed Jars must be processed in the Canning Pot to complete preservation. Once finished, the jar becomes a Preserved Jar — the final state.

How long a Preserved Jar keeps food depends on the lid used. Wooden Lids provide ~10x the normal spoil rate, a Wooden Lid with Beeswax ~12x, and a Metal Lid ~15x. See the lid tier breakdown above for more detail.

*Note: All preservation multiplier values are configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize these values to better fit their world balance.

Opened Jar
────────────────────────
A Preserved Jar that has cooled below 40°C can be opened by holding Shift and Right mouse on the jar. Once opened, the contents are accessible in two ways:

Direct eating: Select the Opened Jar in your hotbar and hold Right mouse. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the jar itself.

Bowl eating: Similar to taking servings out of a crock with a bowl, you can do the same with an opened jar. Simply place the opened jar on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out.

Once all servings have been consumed or removed, the jar automatically returns to an Empty Jar, ready to be refilled and reused.

Note: The preservation bonus only applies while the jar is sealed. Once opened, the meal returns to a normal spoilage rate and should be consumed in a timely manner.

Rotten Jar
────────────────────────
If a Filled, Sealed, or Preserved Jar is left too long without being processed or consumed, its contents will spoil. Once spoilage reaches 100%, the contents become rotten and are no longer edible.

Unlike metal cans, a jar with rotten contents is not permanently damaged and can be cleaned and reused. To do so, first remove the lid if one is applied, then throw the jar into water. The rotten contents will wash out, leaving you with a clean Empty Jar ready to be refilled.

Hot Jars
────────────────────────
Preserved Jars come out of the Canning Pot at high temperature. Use Canning Tongs to handle them safely, and remember that jars must cool below 40°C before they can be opened. See the Hot System guide for full details.

Canning Press
Used to seal Filled Cans before pressure processing.

The Canning Press is the second stage of the canning process. It is used to attach a properly prepared Canning Lid to a Filled Can, creating a Sealed Can ready for pressure cooking.

Slot Layout
────────────────────────
The press contains 3 slots: 2 input slots and 1 output slot.

Top Left Input: Accepts only Canning Lids.
Bottom Left Input: Accepts only Filled Cans.
Right Output Slot: Produces the Sealed Can once pressing is complete.

Using the Press
────────────────────────
The Canning Press has two interaction points. The base plate is used to open the GUI and place items. The upper handle section is used to operate the press.

Loading a Filled Can quickly: With a Filled Can selected in your hotbar, right-click the base plate. If the filled-can slot is empty, the can will be inserted directly without opening the GUI. If the slot is already occupied, the GUI will open as normal.

Operating the press — Hold RMB: With a Filled Can and a Canning Lid inserted, hold Right mouse on the press handle. The screw will lower as the animation progresses. Releasing early cancels the operation. Once the screw reaches the bottom, the process finishes and a Sealed Can is produced in the output slot. Right-click the handle again to raise it back up.

Operating the press — Sneak + RMB: As an alternative, Shift and Right mouse on the handle once. The press will automatically run through the full animation without requiring you to hold the button. Once the screw reaches the bottom, the process finishes and a Sealed Can is produced in the output slot. Right-click the handle again to raise it back up.

Important
────────────────────────
A Sealed Can is not yet preserved. The contents remain raw and will continue to decay at normal spoilage rates. If left unprocessed, a Sealed Can will eventually rot and become a Rotten Can. Sealed Cans must be pressure cooked to complete the preservation process.

Canning Lids
────────────────────────
Canning Lids are produced in multiple stages.

Steel Lid: Crafted from a Steel Bar using a saw in the crafting grid. One Steel Bar produces 32 Steel Lids. Steel Bars are a base game item forged at the anvil.

Steel Lids cannot be used for sealing until treated.

Canning Lid: Steel Lids must be placed in a sealed barrel containing diluted cassiterite. Each lid requires 0.1 liters of solution and takes 24 hours to complete after sealing the barrel. Once finished, they become Canning Lids.

Only Canning Lids can be inserted into the Canning Press. Untreated Steel Lids will not function for sealing.

Pressure Cooker
Used to preserve sealed cans through heat and pressure.

The Pressure Cooker is the final stage of the canning process. It applies sustained high temperature and pressure to Sealed Cans, transforming them into fully preserved meal cans.

Slot Layout
────────────────────────
The Pressure Cooker contains 6 total slots.

Top 4 Input Slots: Accept Sealed Cans only. Each slot holds one can, allowing up to four cans to be processed at once.
Bottom Left Slot: Accepts Firewood. This slot is marked with a fire icon and is used to generate heat.
Bottom Right Slot: Accepts Water. This slot is marked with a water droplet icon and supplies the liquid required for pressure cooking.

Water Requirements
────────────────────────
Each Sealed Can requires 1 liter of water to process. With four can slots available, the Pressure Cooker can store a maximum of 4 liters of water at a time. The correct amount of water must be present before preservation begins.

Temperature & Cooking Time
────────────────────────
The cooker must reach at least 250°C before preservation begins. The required amount of water must also be present at this time.

The cooking process takes 90 seconds. The temperature must remain at or above 250°C and the required water level must remain unchanged for the entire duration. If either the temperature drops below 250°C or the water amount is reduced, the preservation process will stop and reset. Processing will only continue once both the correct temperature and required water amount are restored.

Preserved Cans
────────────────────────
Once finished, Sealed Cans are transformed into Preserved Meal Cans. These cans now contain fully cooked meals based on the ingredients originally placed in the Canning Bench.

The preserved can displays the meal type and nutritional values. A label similar to vanilla sealed crocks will appear, indicating the meal category.

Preserved Cans significantly extend food longevity. While vanilla sealed crocks preserve food at ~10x the normal spoil rate, preserved cans extend this to 25x the normal rate, offering nearly double the long-term storage potential.

*Note: The spoilage multiplier for preserved cans is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Canning Pot
Used to process sealed Glass Jars through heat preservation.

The Canning Pot is the processing station for Glass Jars. It works similarly to the Pressure Cooker but does not require pressurization — just sustained heat and water.

Metal Variants
────────────────────────
Canning Pots come in multiple metal variants: Copper, Tin Bronze, Bismuth Bronze, Black Bronze, Gold, Silver, Iron, Meteoric Iron, and Steel. All variants work the same and differ only in material and appearance.

Slot Layout
────────────────────────
The Canning Pot contains 6 total slots.

Top 4 Input Slots: Accept Sealed Glass Jars only. Each slot holds one jar, allowing up to four jars to be processed at a time.
Bottom Left Slot: Accepts Firewood. This is the fuel slot marked with a fire icon.
Bottom Right Slot: Accepts Water. This slot is marked with a water droplet icon.

Water Requirements
────────────────────────
Each Sealed Glass Jar requires 1 liter of water to process. With four jar slots, the pot can hold a maximum of 4 liters at a time. The correct amount of water must be present before preservation begins.

Temperature & Cooking Time
────────────────────────
The Canning Pot must reach at least 120°C before preservation begins. The required water must also be present at this point.

Processing takes 90 seconds. Both the temperature and water level must remain stable for the full duration — if the temperature drops below 120°C or the water is reduced, the process will stop and reset. It will resume once both conditions are met again.

Important: Hot Jars
────────────────────────
Glass Jars come out of the Canning Pot very hot. Always use Canning Tongs to handle them safely. There is a 15% chance to drop and shatter a hot jar while picking it up without proper tongs. Picking up a hot jar with no tongs will cause you to drop the jar and a 15% chance to shatter the jar. See the Hot System guide for full details.

Canning Tongs
Required for safely handling hot cans and glass jars.

Canning Tongs are purpose-built for removing and handling hot cans and Glass Jars straight out of the Pressure Cooker or Canning Pot. Using the wrong tool — or no tool at all — while handling hot containers puts both you and the container at risk.

Metal Variants
────────────────────────
Canning Tongs come in the same metal variants as the Canning Pot: Copper, Tin Bronze, Bismuth Bronze, Black Bronze, Gold, Silver, Iron, Meteoric Iron, and Steel. All variants work the same.

How to Use
────────────────────────
Equip Canning Tongs in your off-hand before picking up or interacting with any hot can or Glass Jar. With the tongs in hand, hot containers can be handled safely with no risk of dropping or breakage.

Glass Jars — Handling Rules
────────────────────────
Glass Jars are unforgiving when hot. Here is how each scenario plays out:

No tongs equipped: When the jar is dropped there is a 15% chance it shatters, destroying the jar and its contents permanently.

Vanilla tongs equipped: Standard vanilla tongs are not designed for canning work. There is a 15% chance the jar slips, drops, and shatters.

Canning Tongs equipped: Safe handling, no risk of dropping or shattering.

Cans — Handling Rules
────────────────────────
Hot metal cans from the Pressure Cooker are also affected by the heat system. Canning Tongs are recommended for handling them, though cans do not carry the same shattering risk as Glass Jars.

Water Warning
────────────────────────
Warning: Never put a hot Glass Jar into water. The thermal shock will shatter it instantly, destroying the jar and everything inside. Be mindful of water sources when handling freshly processed jars.

Hot System — Temperature & Handling
How heat affects cans and glass jars after processing.

When a can or Glass Jar finishes processing, it comes out of the cooker at high temperature. That heat is tracked on the container itself and determines how it can safely be handled until it cools down.

How It Works
────────────────────────
Once out of the Pressure Cooker or Canning Pot, a container is considered hot until it cools down naturally over time. During this window, how you handle it matters — especially for Glass Jars.

Handling Hot Cans
────────────────────────
Hot metal cans can be handled safely with Canning Tongs. They do not shatter, but it is still a good idea to have tongs ready when pulling cans out of the Pressure Cooker.

Handling Hot Glass Jars
────────────────────────
Glass Jars need proper Canning Tongs to handle safely once hot. Getting it wrong has real consequences:

Without tongs: When the jar is dropped there is a 15% chance of shattering, permanently destroying the jar and its contents.

With vanilla tongs: Still not safe. Vanilla tongs were not made for this and there is a 15% chance the jar slips, drops, and shatters.

With Canning Tongs: Safe. No risk of dropping or shattering.

Contact with water: Dropping or throwing a hot Glass Jar into water causes immediate thermal shock. The jar will shatter and its contents are lost. Stay clear of water when handling hot jars.

Cooling Down
────────────────────────
Containers cool down on their own over time once away from the heat source. Once fully cooled, they can be picked up and handled normally. If you do not have Canning Tongs on hand, waiting for things to cool is always an option.

Tip: Get your Canning Tongs ready before you start a processing run so they are within reach the moment the jars or cans come out.

Can Opener
Required to open Preserved Meal Cans.

The Can Opener is the only tool capable of opening preserved meal cans. Without it, preserved cans cannot be accessed or consumed.

How to Use
────────────────────────
To open a preserved can, place the Can Opener in your off-hand and select a Preserved Can in your hotbar.

Hold Shift and Right mouse while holding the preserved can. After approximately 3 seconds, the can will open.

Crafting
────────────────────────
The Can Opener is crafted by combining a Can Opener Toolhead and a Stick in the crafting grid.

Can Opener Toolhead: Forged at the anvil using 1 Steel Ingot. The toolhead must be completed through the smithing process before it can be assembled into a functional tool.

Durability
────────────────────────
The Can Opener has a durability of 50. Each can opened consumes 1 durability. A single Can Opener can therefore open up to 50 cans before it breaks and must be replaced.

Opening Result
────────────────────────
Once opened, the can changes visually to display its contents and a cracked lid. The meal inside is now accessible in two ways:

Direct eating: Select the Opened Can in your hotbar and hold Right mouse. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the can itself.

Bowl eating: Similar to taking servings out of a crock with a bowl, you can do the same with an opened can. Simply place the opened can on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out.

Once all servings have been consumed or removed, the can automatically reverts to an Empty Can and can be refilled at the Canning Bench.

Note: The 25× preservation bonus only applies while the can is sealed. Once opened, the meal returns to a normal spoilage rate and should be consumed in a timely manner.

Accessing Preserved Food — Glass Jars
How to open and consume food from a Preserved Glass Jar.

Unlike metal cans which require a Can Opener, Glass Jars are opened by hand — but only once they have cooled down enough to be safe. Attempting to open a jar while it is still hot is not possible, as the contents have not yet fully settled and the seal is unsafe to break.

Handling While Hot

When a hot jar is dropped there is a 15% chance it will shatter, permanently destroying the jar and its contents. Using vanilla tongs is not a safe alternative — with the wrong tongs there is a 15% chance the jar will slip, drop, and shatter. Always use Canning Tongs to handle hot jars safely.

How to Open
────────────────────────
Once the jar has cooled below 40°C, place it on the ground, a table, or a shelf. Then hold Shift and Right mouse on the jar to pop the lid off. The jar will open and its contents will become accessible.

Opening Result
────────────────────────
Once opened, the jar changes visually to display its contents with the lid removed. The meal inside is now accessible in two ways:

Direct eating: Select the Opened Jar in your hotbar and hold Right mouse. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the jar itself.

Bowl eating: Similar to taking servings out of a crock with a bowl, you can do the same with an opened jar. Simply place the opened jar on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out.

Once all servings have been consumed or removed, the jar automatically returns to an Empty Jar, ready to be refilled and reused at the Canning Bench.

Note: The preservation bonus only applies while the jar is sealed. Once opened, the meal returns to a normal spoilage rate and should be consumed in a timely manner.

Troubleshooting
Common issues and how to resolve them.

The Canning Bench will not produce a Filled Can or Jar
────────────────────────
- Ensure an Empty Can or Glass Jar is placed in the correct slot.
- Verify that all four ingredient slots contain valid raw ingredients.
- Confirm the ingredient ratios match a valid base game meal.
- Refer to Cooking Recipes for correct combinations and ratios.

The Canning Press will not seal the can
────────────────────────
- Ensure a Filled Can is placed in the Bottom Left slot.
- Ensure a Canning Lid (not a Steel Lid) is placed in the Top Left slot.
- To operate: hold right-click on the handle until the screw fully lowers, or Sneak + right-click once to let it run automatically.
- Once the screw reaches the bottom, the process finishes and a Sealed Can is produced in the output slot.
- Right-click the handle again to raise it back up before starting the next operation.

I cannot apply a lid to my Glass Jar
────────────────────────
- Lids are not applied through the Canning Press. They are applied directly to a jar placed in the world.
- Place the jar on the ground, or a table.
- Select the lid you want to use in your active hotbar slot.
- Hold Shift and Right mouse to apply the lid.
- If you want to change the lid, remove it first by doing the same with an empty hotbar slot, then apply the new one.
- Once the lid is on, right-click the jar to pick it up.

I cannot apply beeswax to my Wooden Lid jar
────────────────────────
- Beeswax can only be applied to jars that already have a Wooden Lid in place. Metal Lid jars cannot be sealed with beeswax.
- Hold beeswax in your active hotbar slot and right-click the jar. This works whether the jar is placed on the ground, stored on a shelf, or in ground storage.
- If nothing happens, check that the jar has not already been sealed with beeswax — it can only be applied once.

My Sealed Can spoiled
────────────────────────
A Sealed Can is not yet preserved. The contents remain raw and will spoil at normal rates unless processed in the Pressure Cooker. If left too long, the contents will become rotten and the can will be permanently damaged.

The Pressure Cooker is not preserving my cans
────────────────────────
- Ensure only Sealed Cans are placed in the top slots.
- Add at least 1 liter of water per can (maximum 4 liters total).
- Insert Firewood in the fuel slot.
- The temperature must reach and remain at or above 250°C.
- The cooker must maintain 250°C for the full 90 seconds in order to complete preservation.

The Canning Pot is not preserving my jars
────────────────────────
- Ensure only Sealed Glass Jars are placed in the top slots.
- Add at least 1 liter of water per jar (maximum 4 liters total).
- Insert Firewood in the fuel slot.
- The temperature must reach and remain at or above 120°C.
- The pot must maintain 120°C for the full 90 seconds in order to complete preservation.

My Preserved Can is spoiling quickly
────────────────────────
The 25× preservation bonus only applies while the can is sealed. Once opened, the meal returns to normal spoilage rates.

My Preserved Jar is spoiling faster than expected
────────────────────────
Check which lid was used when sealing. Wooden Lids give ~10x, a Wooden Lid with Beeswax gives ~12x, and a Metal Lid gives ~15x. If longer storage is needed, try sealing with a different lid next time or consider switching to the Metal Can system for the full 25x rate.

I cannot open my can
────────────────────────
- Place the Can Opener in your off-hand.
- Select the Preserved Can in your hotbar.
- Hold Shift and Right mouse for approximately 3 seconds.
- Ensure the Can Opener has remaining durability.

I cannot open my Glass Jar
────────────────────────
- Glass Jars must cool to below 40°C before they can be opened. Check the jar's temperature by hovering over it and wait until it has cooled sufficiently.
- To open, place the jar on the ground, a table, or a shelf.
- Hold Shift and Right mouse on the jar to pop the lid off.

I opened my can, how do I eat from it?
────────────────────────
- Direct eating: Select the Opened Can in your hotbar and hold right-click. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the can itself.
- Bowl eating: Place the opened can on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out, just like a crock.
- Once all servings are gone, the can automatically returns to an Empty Can.

I opened my jar, how do I eat from it?
────────────────────────
- Direct eating: Select the Opened Jar in your hotbar and hold right-click. This works just like eating from a bowl, except you eat directly from the jar itself.
- Bowl eating: Place the opened jar on the ground, a table, or a shelf, then right-click it with a bowl in hand to take a serving out, just like a crock.
- Once all servings are gone, the jar automatically returns to an Empty Jar.

My Glass Jar has rotten contents, how do I clean it?
────────────────────────
Unlike metal cans, Glass Jars can be cleaned and reused after the contents have rotted.
- If the jar has a lid on it, remove it first by placing the jar down and using an empty hotbar slot with Shift and Right mouse.
- Once the lid is removed, throw the jar into water. The rotten contents will wash out and you will be left with a clean Empty Jar ready to be refilled.

My Glass Jar shattered
────────────────────────
Hot Glass Jars that are dropped have a 15% chance of shattering and cannot be recovered. Always use Canning Tongs when handling freshly processed jars. Filled Cans and Sealed Cans will spoil if not processed in time. Once the contents reach full spoilage, they become rotten and contamination permanently damages the container. Rotten Cans cannot be reused for food preservation.

Populating Your First Worms
A complete guide to raising your own worm supply.

The Worm Bin turns bedding, food, moisture, and a handful of starter worms into a renewing source of bait. There are two bins: the Simple Worm Bin Simple Worm Bin (crafted from boards - larger and faster) and the Crude Worm Bin Crude Worm Bin (a cheap early-game starter). Both work the same way; only their numbers differ.

Getting Started
────────────────────────
A bin needs four basics before it will produce:

Bedding: add soil for regular worms, or any type of sand for Sea Worms. The Simple Worm Bin needs 3 bedding additions; the Crude Worm Bin needs 1.
Food: rot or compost. The Simple bin holds 8 food; the Crude bin holds 4.
Moisture: rain increases moisture in the bin, or you can increase moisture with a ceramic watering can or water from a bucket. If you use sand, the bin needs saltwater from a bucket.
Starter worms: add vanilla worms gathered with worm grunting. The Simple bin needs 4 starter worms; the Crude bin needs 2.

Once all four are in place the bin begins working on its own. Right-click with an empty hand to collect the worms it has made.

Note: The food capacity and starter colony size, for both bins, are configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize these values to better fit their world balance.

Producing Worms
────────────────────────
Every 3 in-game hours the bin runs a production cycle. Each cycle makes 2 worms in the Simple bin (1 in the Crude bin) and uses up 1 food. Production continues only while the bin has bedding, food, and moisture, and stops once the bin is full of worms - the Simple bin holds 16, the Crude bin 4.

Harvesting never removes your starter colony, so a stocked bin keeps producing indefinitely as long as you keep it fed and moist. Finished worms can also pop out of the soil in the bin, similar to worm grunting; collect those directly when you see them.

Note: The production interval, worms produced per cycle, and storage cap, for both bins, are configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize these values to better fit their world balance.

Moisture & Temperature
────────────────────────
Bedding dries out over time and must stay damp to produce. A full soak lasts about 4 in-game days. If the bin is open to the sky, rain increases moisture in the bin. You can also increase moisture with a ceramic watering can or water from a bucket.

Production also pauses at 0 C or colder. Keep the bin somewhere temperate and it will run year-round.

Worm Types & Bonuses
────────────────────────
Vanilla Worms. A bin with soil and rot produces vanilla worms - the same worms gathered through worm grunting.

Nightcrawlers. If you apply compost instead of rot, the bin produces Live Nightcrawler Nightcrawlers, a larger bait, and gains a +5% R3D Worm chance. One compost counts as 4 food. A bin commits to one food type while it holds food or worms; empty it to switch.

R3D Worms. Bins using soil can sometimes produce a rare Live R3D Worm R3D Worm as a bonus output. The base chance is 10% in the Simple bin and 5% in the Crude bin. Better soil used as bedding adds more chance:
- Low fertility soil: +0% per soil
- Medium fertility soil: +1% per soil
- High fertility soil: +2% per soil
- Terra preta: +3% per soil
Compost-fed bins gain another +5%. For example, a Simple bin with three Terra preta soil additions adds +9%; feeding compost makes the total R3D chance 24%.

Sea Worms. Using any type of sand instead of soil makes the bin produce Live Sea Worm Sea Worms. If you use sand, the bin requires saltwater from a bucket; a watering can and freshwater bucket will not work. They do not produce R3D Worms, and bedding types cannot be mixed.

Note: The base R3D Worm chance for both bins is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib; the soil-fertility and compost bonuses are fixed. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Feeding Your Worms
Using the Compost Bin to prepare rot and compost for worm bins.

The Compost Bin Compost Bin is a simple storage bin for turning spare perishables into rot faster. It has 16 slots, and food stored inside perishes at 4x speed.

Note: The Compost Bin perish-speed factor is configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize this value to better fit their world balance.

Using the Bin
────────────────────────
Use Right mouse on the Compost Bin to open its inventory, then place food or other perishables inside. As the contents spoil, they become rot much sooner than they would in normal storage.

The lid opens automatically when you open the bin and closes again when you are done. The lid is visual only; the bin works as long as items are stored inside.

For Worm Bins

A Worm Bin commits to one food type while it still holds food or produced worms. Empty the bin before switching between rot and compost.

Baits and Fish
Choosing which worm to use for different fish.

Expanded Fishing adds several worm baits for fishing rods and Fish Traps. Each bait has a role based on water type and fish size, so matching the bait to the fish matters.

Bait Types
────────────────────────
Live worm Vanilla Worms: Standard worm bait gathered through worm grunting, or produced from a bin using soil and rot. They can catch small and medium fish where ordinary worm bait is accepted.

Live Nightcrawler Nightcrawlers: Larger freshwater bait. They can catch medium freshwater fish such as bass, carp, catfish, pickerel, salmon, tilapia, and walleye.

Live R3D Worm R3D Worms: Strong bait for medium and large fish in both freshwater and saltwater areas. In freshwater, they can catch medium fish such as bass, carp, catfish, pickerel, salmon, tilapia, and walleye, plus pike. In saltwater, they can catch amberjack, barracuda, mahi-mahi, grouper, salmon, snapper, tuna, wolf fish, and wreckfish.

Live Sea Worm Sea Worms: Saltwater-focused bait. They work on medium and large saltwater fish, including amberjack, barracuda, mahi-mahi, grouper, salmon, snapper, tuna, wolf fish, and wreckfish.

Scented Worm Scented Worms: Bait for the largest fish in any area. Make one by cooking 1 R3D Worm with 2 fennel and 1 litre of water. They can catch freshwater arapaima and sheatfish, plus saltwater coelacanth and sturgeon.

Vanilla Worms: small and medium fish.
Nightcrawlers: medium freshwater fish.
R3D Worms: medium and large fish in freshwater or saltwater areas.
Sea Worms: medium and large saltwater fish.
Scented Worms: the largest fish in freshwater or saltwater areas.

Note: This guide lists the main bait roles added by Expanded Fishing. Vanilla bait such as meat, fish, stinkmeat, and stinkdough still follows the base game fish rules.

Catching Live Fish
Using Fish Traps to passively catch live fish.

Fish Traps are placed in water and baited with worms. Once baited, a trap periodically checks the local water, climate, fish population, and bait type to decide what can be caught there, similar to how vanilla fishing chooses fish when using a fishing rod.

Trap Types
────────────────────────
Simple Fish Trap Simple Fish Trap: A two-block trap for small and medium fish. It needs a stick to hold bait, then one worm bait. It holds 1 fish.

Large Simple Fish Trap Large Simple Fish Trap: A three-block trap that can catch every fish size. It also needs a stick, then one worm bait, and holds 1 fish.

Reef Fish Trap Reef Fish Trap: A compact trap for tiny reef fish. It does not use a stick. Add 2 worms to bait it, and it can hold up to 3 fish.

Baiting and Collecting
────────────────────────
For Simple and Large traps, use Right mouse with a stick first, then use Right mouse with a worm bait. The bait is spent when a fish bites.

For Reef traps, use Right mouse with worm bait until two worms are loaded. The two worms stay in the trap until the trap fills.

Use an empty hand with Right mouse to collect caught fish. If the trap has no fish, the same empty-hand interaction gives back loaded bait or the stick where applicable.

How Catches Work
────────────────────────
A baited trap attempts a catch every 2 in-game hours by default. If an eligible fish bites, the default catch chance is 80%. If the fish gets away, the bait is still used.

Traps need a large enough connected body of water, at least 100 water blocks. They also follow the same kind of local fish rules as rod fishing: the fish must fit the water type, climate, regional fish population, trap size, and bait.

Caught fish appear alive inside the trap while you are nearby, then can be collected as items. You can use live fish to make your own aquarium, or kill one when you are ready to use it as food. Placed live fish show Placed Live Fish when looked at, so you can tell they came from your catch.

Moving and Naming Live Fish
────────────────────────
Fish Net Fish Nets pick up placed live fish so you can move them. Look at a placed live fish and use Left mouse with the net. The net scoops the fish without harming it. The net only works on placed live fish, and each pickup uses 5 durability. The Reinforced Fish Net Reinforced Fish Net lasts longer.

Fish Tag Fish Tags name live fish. Place the live fish in your offhand, hold a Fish Tag in your main hand, then use Sneak + Right mouse. Enter a name and save it. The tag is consumed, and the fish tooltip changes to Aquarium Fish: Name. The name stays with the fish when it is placed and picked back up with a net.

To kill a live fish after collecting it, place the fish in your offhand, hold a knife in your main hand, then use Sneak + Right mouse. See Fillet Knives for the fillet knife bonuses.

Note: The catch interval and catch chance are configurable in the mod configuration file via ConfigLib. Server owners may customize these values to better fit their world balance.

Hungry Visitors
Keeping chickens and raccoons from raiding your worm bins.

A stocked Worm Bin counts as an animal food source. Chickens and raccoons can path to it and eat stored worms if they can reach the bin.

What They Take
────────────────────────
Hungry visitors only care about worms the bin has already produced. They do not remove bedding, food, moisture, or the starter colony.

If visible worms have popped out of the soil in the bin, an animal may eat one of those. If no visible worm is available, it can still take one stored worm from the bin.

How to Protect a Bin
────────────────────────
Keep worm bins behind fences, walls, or closed doors so chickens and raccoons cannot path to them. The bin can keep producing normally as long as you can still reach it to feed, moisten, and harvest it.

Bins with no stored worms are not worth raiding, but once production starts, nearby animals may notice them. If worms seem to disappear before you collect them, check for animals with access to the bin.

Tip: Treat worm bins like farmland when animals are nearby. A simple fence around the work area is usually enough.

The Fishing Logbook
Recording your catches, discoveries, and favorite fishing spots.

The Fishing Logbook Fishing Logbook is a personal journal for tracking every fish you catch. All notes are stored in the book itself, so it keeps its records when stored, dropped, or handed to another player. The first player to open a new logbook becomes its owner, and the book takes their name.

Getting Started
────────────────────────
Hold the logbook and use Right mouse to open it. When the book opens, it automatically notes the current date, season, and your coordinates for the next entry. Each can be changed with its Edit button if you are logging a catch from earlier or elsewhere.

The book has six tabs along the top: Overview, Fish Checklist, Bait Notes, Aquarium Notes, Recents, and Trophy.

Logging a Catch
────────────────────────
Catches are recorded manually in the Fish Checklist tab. Select the fish from the list. The filter tabs narrow the list down to Freshwater, Saltwater, Reef, or already-Discovered fish. Then fill in the details on the right: color variant (for fish with two looks), life stage, time of day, bait used, and whether it was caught with a fishing rod or fish trap.

The Mark Location toggle chooses whether this catch is pinned on your world map. Press Log Catch to save the entry. The fish is then marked Discovered with a checkmark in the list, and its record tracks how many times you have caught it, the first catch date, and the most recent details. Discovered fish can also be starred as a favorite in their detail panel.

The Tabs
────────────────────────
Overview: your discovery progress toward all 56 species, catch totals, favorite bait, recent catches, per-water-type progress, and your most caught fish.

Fish Checklist: the full species list with pictures, details for each fish such as size, water type, and which baits it takes, plus the Log Catch controls.

Bait Notes: a reference table of every bait and what it is best for.

Aquarium Notes: a checklist of your caught fish where you can mark which ones you have preserved with taxidermy and which are living in your aquarium.

Taming Guide: General Concept

This guide is an attempt to explain the taming mechanics introduced by the "Pet AI" mod.

Pet AI itself does not introduce any tameable creatures. It is just a framework for other mods to make creating pets more easy. Most pets will be able to receive commands by the player. To give your pet a command, you need to crouch right click on it. A small GUI will open containing the various commands your pet will accept. But be aware, as your pet will only execute commands if you are a good pet owner. That generally means feeding your pet regularly, but can also be expanded to engaging in playful activities with it.

Pet AI currently supports four different aggression levels for pets:
Passive: Your pet won't harm anybody.
Neutral: Your pet will only attack if provoked.
Protective: Your pet will fight along your side, it will defend you from evil creatures and hunt down your victims.
Aggressive: Your pet will attack a small selection of creatures on its own.

If you feel the urge to try and remote control your pet, check out the pet whistle. It also makes your pet more useful when hunting.
Check out the pet cushions too. They are purely decorative but sometimes your pets will sleep in them.

Convergence Gates

A player-built Conflux circuit contains a rift for linked travel, exploration, or death recovery. Its installed Core determines its function.

Structure and Placement
Build a five-block-wide by five-block-tall outer frame around a clear three-by-three opening. Place a Rift Containment Brace at each corner. Fill the remaining perimeter with eleven Conflux Frame Blocks and one Convergence Core Housing. The Housing can replace any of the twelve non-corner Frame positions, including the top or bottom. Face its control panel outward and orient the Frame conduits along the perimeter. A wrench rotates Frames and Braces. The Housing's power stripe follows its horizontal or vertical frame position.

Choose the Appearance
Use the style selector in the Core Housing to choose the Circular Gate or Original Gate. Both use the same structure and travel rules. The circular design uses a segmented hoop matching the Storm Stabilizer, with light channels on both faces. When powered, its sections assemble outward from the Housing in two directions and then begin rotating. On power loss, the hoop slows and retracts.

Linked Travel
Install one Stabilized Rift Core and a charged Temporal Crystal with enough energy for a jump in each Gate. A complete frame powers up in stages and forms a blue rift. Use the Housing to select another available Gate, then walk into the rift. Both endpoints must be complete, powered, and accessible. A distant destination is loaded on demand when a traveler enters the departure rift, so connection may take a moment. The departure Gate spends one configured Crystal jump; the receiving Gate pays no arrival cost. By default, one jump costs five minutes from a 30-minute Crystal, allowing six departures per full Crystal. An open Gate does not drain charge while idle.

Naming and Access
New Housings receive a location-based name so Gate lists are easier to distinguish. Rename yours in the Housing. The owner can choose Public or Private access and list allowed players. Removing a Housing removes its Gate from the registry. An incomplete, unpowered, obstructed, or inaccessible destination cannot be used for travel.

Safety and Indicators
Arrival space is checked on both sides of the destination. If no safe exit exists, travel is blocked, the conduits turn red, and a warning pulse circles the frame. Clear the destination to restore cyan. Dark conduits mean inactive; cyan conduits and a clockwise pulse mean powered. Removing a Core or Crystal collapses the portal. Failed arrival refunds reserved Crystal charge.

Exploration
A natural Rift Core provides random Exploration Rift travel instead of a paired link. That process consumes the Core and returns an empty Containment Core. It is separate from the reusable Crystal budget for paired travel. Travelers with the optional Rift Recall ability can receive an orange return rift after this journey, just as after natural blue-rift travel.

Recovery
A Recovery Core and charged Crystal arm the Gate for its owner's next death in the same dimension. Purple means awaiting that death; orange means a recorded return is ready. The waiting portal cannot transport anyone. Only the owner can use the recovery return. Read the Recovery Core entry for the offering, saved death locations, and arrival protection.

Recharging
A Gate without enough charge for another jump shuts down and retains its Crystal. Remove it through the Housing and top it up in the Rift Resonance Array. The inventory briefly locks during transit to keep the reserved charge attached to its Crystal.

Owner Controls
Only the owner manages settings and installed items. Visitors see destination, travel status, and charge, but not configuration. Add Player lists known players who previously joined this server, including offline players; manual names remain supported. Private access and allowed players persist across saves. Access is checked at both Gates.

Ownership Transfer and Protection
Select a known player and confirm Transfer Ownership. Remove any Recovery Core and finish pending travel first. The former owner loses management rights and needs explicit permission to use a Private Gate. Only the owner or a server admin with controlserver privilege can dismantle a claimed Gate, including its Housing, Frames, and Braces. Land-claim restrictions still apply.

Standby and Safety
Destination Standby means the remote Gate needs loading, not necessarily a broken link. Enter the rift and wait for Loading Destination. Offline reasons and remaining jumps help identify missing power or other problems. Keep both exits clear with solid footing and headroom. Access, charge, link, and landing are checked again before departure. Leaving the portal cancels pending travel.

Dimensional Travel
A green Dimensional Core opens The Fractured Deep rather than a paired link. Read its entry for entry, return, and respawn behavior.

Temporal Anchor

An Anchor begins as a private, unassigned foundation. Placement starts a five-second calibration and binds the foundation to its owner.

Choosing a Role
After calibration, install one Temporal Crystal to specialize the foundation as a charged Travel Anchor, or install one Cargo Transmitter to create an 18-slot Cargo Anchor. Each player may own one Travel Anchor and one Cargo Anchor, and either role may be established first.

Travel Anchor
The Temporal Triangulator's Anchor mode detects your Travel Anchor and reports its direction, distance, charge, and travel readiness. When Travel reports Ready, hold use and remain still through synchronization. Successful controlled travel returns you beside the Anchor. An uncharged Crystal is consumed for one return; a charged Crystal spends one sixth of its full capacity per return and remains reusable.

Relocating Foundations and Travel Anchors
Hold Sneak while placing another Anchor to relocate your existing unassigned foundation or Travel Anchor remotely. This is a relocation: the Anchor item is not consumed. A Travel Anchor retains its installed Crystal and charge while recalibrating at the new location.

Breaking a Travel Anchor
Breaking a Travel Anchor manually returns its installed Crystal, including a depleted reusable Crystal, to the breaker. It enters inventory when space is available or drops at the Anchor. Explosions and unusual removal can still destroy the charge.

Cargo Anchor Restriction
Cargo Anchors cannot be relocated remotely. Visit the Cargo Anchor, resolve pending deliveries, empty it, and break it manually before creating another. Breaking it returns the installed Cargo Transmitter.

The temporal network recognizes one destination of each specialized role per traveler.

Crystal Charge
A fully charged Crystal holds 30 minutes of energy by default. Item and machine information shows remaining time and available jumps. Server settings can change the full duration. Anchor and paired Gate travel each require one sixth of a full charge: five minutes by default, allowing six jumps from a full Crystal. Charge also spent in a Temporal Drive reduces the jumps available. A partially charged Crystal with less than one jump remaining must be topped up before travel.

Disposable and Reusable Crystals
An uncharged Crystal powers one Anchor return and is consumed by that jump. A charged Crystal instead spends one sixth of its full capacity per return and remains reusable after depletion. Failed travel refunds reserved charge. Sneak-use the Anchor with an empty hand to remove its reusable Crystal, then recharge it in the Rift Resonance Array. Remove the installed reusable Crystal before inserting another or converting the Anchor to cargo. A partially charged Crystal needs enough energy for a whole jump to be installed.

Distant Destinations
Travel requests load the destination chunk on demand. Allow synchronization to finish; loading does not bypass charge, access, or safe-arrival checks.

Temporal Cargo

Temporal Cargo uses the same Cargo Transmitter at both ends of a private cargo link. One Transmitter is installed into an Anchor as the receiving endpoint; another is placed in the field to send ordinary item stacks, including across dimensions when the destination becomes available.

Creating the Destination
Craft a Cargo Transmitter, place an Anchor foundation, and wait for its short calibration. Install the Transmitter into the foundation to convert it into an 18-slot Cargo Anchor. A Temporal Crystal instead specializes the foundation as your Travel Anchor. You may maintain one Travel Anchor and one Cargo Anchor, and either may be constructed first.

Binding a Field Transmitter
Craft and place a second Cargo Transmitter, select Cargo Anchor mode on the Temporal Triangulator, and use the Triangulator on the Transmitter to bind it to your calibrated Cargo Anchor. Each field Transmitter provides six staging slots and requires no Temporal Crystal fuel.

Sending Cargo
Place up to six ordinary item stacks in the field Transmitter. With the Temporal Triangulator still in Cargo Anchor mode, stand within six blocks and hold the scanner use button until the HUD transmission bar completes. You do not need to point at the Transmitter. Releasing early cancels without moving cargo. The complete batch is secured before it leaves. The destination chunk loads on demand, even across long distances or dimensions. If the Cargo Anchor has enough room, the entire shipment arrives together. Otherwise, it remains safely pending and retries when delivery becomes possible.

Relocation
Cargo Anchors cannot be replaced remotely because doing so could move stored items without cargo transmission. To establish one elsewhere, travel to the current Cargo Anchor, resolve all pending deliveries, empty it, and break it manually. Breaking it returns the installed Cargo Transmitter. Unassigned foundations and Travel Anchors may instead be relocated by holding Sneak while placing another Anchor.

Safety
Delivery is atomic: a full destination never receives only part of a batch. An endpoint with an undelivered shipment cannot be broken. Free enough Cargo Anchor space for the complete shipment before attempting to remove either endpoint.

Compatibility
Normal items, blocks, tools, food, and supported stack attributes may be transported. Filled buckets, backpacks, portable inventories, and other nested-content containers are intentionally unsupported.

Temporal Drive

The Temporal Drive converts energy from an installed Temporal Crystal into mechanical torque using Vintage Story's standard mechanical network. A full Crystal provides 30 minutes of operation by default; the server can configure this duration.

Placement and Connection
Place the Drive with its front cartridge facing you. Connect an axle to its mechanical output using normal mechanical placement and connection rules. The Drive may be placed and connected while empty.

Installing a Crystal
Use a Crystal with remaining charge on the front cartridge to install it; empty Crystals are rejected. The glass closes, the internal gear and temporal effects activate, and the Drive begins supplying torque. Use the cartridge with an empty hand to retrieve the Crystal; an empty Drive contributes no power or resistance.

Torque and Speed
One Drive supplies a modest amount of torque up to its operating speed. Additional Drives connected anywhere on the same mechanical network add their torque together, helping the network carry heavier machinery. Stacking Drives does not directly multiply rotational speed. Use vanilla large and small gears when the network needs a different balance of speed and torque.

Using a Drive with Wind Power
A Drive may share a network with a windmill. While the network is below the Drive's operating speed, it assists with torque. If the windmill is already turning the network faster, the Drive freewheels instead of slowing it down. Its position on the connected network does not change this behavior.

Network Changes
Adding or removing axles, gears, sails, machines, or Drives causes the vanilla mechanical network to recalculate. A brief adjustment in rotation can be normal while the network settles.

Multiple Drives increase available torque; gearing determines how that torque is traded for speed.

Depletion and Recharging
Charge drains continuously while the loaded Drive is running, including when no load is connected or the Drive is freewheeling. Time spent paused or unloaded is not charged. At zero, mechanical output, the gear animation, and powered effects stop; the Crystal stays in the cartridge. Use an empty hand to retrieve it. Removal and reinsertion preserve remaining time. Recharge empty or partially used Crystals in the Rift Resonance Array. Hover over the Drive or Crystal to check remaining charge.

Temporal Retort

The Temporal Retort is a specialized two-section laboratory vessel used to perform advanced heated reactions. Its ceramic vessel stands on the left and its firebox extends to the right when viewed from the front.

Construction
1. Use fire clay and clay forming to make an Unfired Retort Vessel and an Unfired Retort Firebox.
2. Fire both components in a pit kiln to produce a Fired Retort Vessel and Fired Retort Firebox.
3. Reinforce the fired vessel in a 3 by 3 crafting grid:

Empty | Empty | Empty
Fireclay Brick | Fired Vessel | Fireclay Brick
Fireclay Brick | Fireclay Brick | Fireclay Brick

This requires five Fireclay Bricks and produces one Reinforced Retort Vessel.

4. Assemble the complete Retort in a 3 by 3 crafting grid:

Empty | Temporal Gear | Empty
Empty | Barrel | Empty
2 Bronze Plates | Reinforced Vessel | Fired Firebox

The two plates may be Tin Bronze, Bismuth Bronze, or Black Bronze.

Placement and Heating
Place the Retort with enough clear horizontal space for both sections. The firebox side may be empty or contain a Firepit. Place and ignite a fueled Firepit inside the firebox to supply heat.

Unlike a standard Barrel, the Retort can safely contain liquids while applying sustained heat. Some Temporal reactions require significant heat before they can begin, and certain processes require the vessel to be clamped shut.

Liquid Handling
The Retort stores a liquid reaction medium and supports many familiar Barrel liquid interactions. Use compatible liquid containers to transfer liquids while the vessel is open.

Protocol Discovery
Some products are known to be craftable even when their exact Retort protocol remains hidden. A protocol is discovered only after you successfully complete it. Use /rt discoveries to review your discoveries.

Server Operator Recipe Maker
Players with the controlserver privilege can open this Retort and enable Snapshot Recipe Maker mode. Its GUI stages recipes with Creative items, exact liquid controls, temperature, duration, lid requirements, default or custom discovery hints, visual input alternatives, preview, and server-side testing. Generated recipes can be created, edited, duplicated, reviewed, or removed while the server is running. Removing one also removes its connected generated discovery pages.

Further Research
As additional Temporal research is uncovered, new recipes and reaction processes may become available.

Additional Temporal reactions and laboratory processes will become available as your knowledge expands.

IndustrialStory Compatibility
With IndustrialStory installed, ordinary Firepits keep its 600-degree cap. A correctly fitted Retort can use the hotter fuel temperature for its reactions even when the Firepit interface still displays 600 degrees. Check the Retort temperature and protocol requirements rather than the Firepit display alone.

Temporal Storm Stabilizer
A Conflux multiblock that creates a spherical refuge whenever its field is powered. Its removable Stabilized Rift Core powers articulated arms and rotating containment rings; four optional Temporal Crystals extend the shield. The visible cyan shell marks the same boundary used for protection.

Getting the Machine
Craft one packed Stabilizer in a 3 x 3 crafting grid using 12 Conflux Iron Plates, 8 Conflux Iron Rods, 8 Containment Insulators, 4 Conflux Binding Compound, 4 Temporal Glass blocks, and 2 Temporal Gears. Top row: 4 Plates | 8 Rods | 4 Plates. Middle row: 8 Insulators | 2 Gears | 4 Temporal Glass. Bottom row: 2 Plates | 4 Binding Compound | 2 Plates. The output is the packed controller; install a Stabilized Rift Core and optional Temporal Crystals separately after unpacking.

Placement and Assembly
Prepare a clear, dry 9 x 9 footprint with solid support under every floor position. The central 5 x 5 must be clear for five blocks of total machine height, counting the base layer. The four corners require two blocks of total height. Place the controller at the centre; its front faces you. The base extends, conduits and pedestals form, and the central machinery rises through a mechanical and temporal reconstruction sequence. Wait for assembly to finish before installing the core.

Install the Containment Core
Right-click the main machine while holding one Stabilized Rift Core. A natural Rift Core or empty Containment Core cannot power it. Stabilized Cores come from capturing a blue Convergence Rift with a prepared Rift Harvester; see Temporal Triangulation and Rift Travel. The core remains removable and is not consumed during operation.

Controls and Automatic Operation
With the core installed, the Stabilizer starts automatically during a temporal storm and shuts down when the storm ends. Empty-hand right-click on the main machine manually starts or stops it. Manually stopping during a storm holds off automatic restart for that storm; manually starting again overrides the hold. Manual operation outside a storm provides the same instability protection, hostile spawn prevention, enemy damage, and boundary effects.

To retrieve the core, stop the machine and wait until the rings and arms have fully folded. Then sneak-right-click the main machine with an empty hand. Pedestals have their own interactions, so aim at the central structure for these controls.

Crystal Pedestals
Each corner pedestal accepts one Temporal Crystal. Right-click an empty pedestal with a Crystal to install it; right-click an occupied pedestal with an empty hand to retrieve it. Crystals may be empty, partially charged, or full, and can be mixed freely. They retain their charge when removed. The Stabilizer currently does not drain Crystal charge or recharge Crystals. Use a Rift Resonance Array and a natural Rift Core for recharging.

Read the pedestal or item information to check remaining charge. A luminous Crystal is not necessarily fully charged.

Shield Radius
At full field strength, default protection extends 16 blocks from the field centre with no Crystals. Each installed Crystal adds 4 blocks even when empty, plus up to 8 more blocks proportional to its charge.

No Crystals: 16-block radius.
Four empty Crystals: 32-block radius.
Four half-charged Crystals: 48-block radius.
Four fully charged Crystals: 64-block radius.
One full, one half-charged, one empty, and one vacant pedestal: 40-block radius.

These are radii, not diameters. Default full-strength radius = 16 + 4 per installed Crystal + 8 times the sum of their charge fractions, capped at 64. Server configuration can change these values. Removing or replacing a Crystal changes the available radius.

The field grows smoothly as it builds strength and contracts as it powers down. During those transitions, only the area inside the current shell is protected. The shield is a complete sphere centred two blocks above the controller base, and also extends below the machine; it is not a flat cylinder or a dome ending at the floor.

What Protection Does
Protection requires an active field and works both during and outside temporal storms. Inside the sphere, personal temporal stability is held at its existing value instead of draining. Low-stability damage and temporal instability effects are suppressed. Storm ambience and visual effects ease away, and the stability gear slows over roughly two and a half seconds. Crossing an active field boundary plays a sound and a brief temporal particle effect, even during manual operation outside a storm.

This pauses instability; it does not refill stored stability. Leaving the sphere restores normal exposure and your previous stability continues from there. Ordinary weather is not removed.

New hostile spawns, including storm creatures, are prevented inside the active protection zone whenever the field is powered. Existing enemies can still enter. Whenever the shield is active, Bells, Bowtorns, Drifters, Locusts, and Shivers inside it take fire damage (0.5 per second); animals and other NPCs are unaffected by this damage. Overlapping shields do not stack the damage. An enemy from these families killed by the shield has a 10% chance to drop one Temporal Residue instead of its normal loot; its corpse provides no ordinary harvest loot. Player kills and unrelated damage retain normal drops, even after earlier shield damage. The shield is not a solid wall and does not grant general immunity to attacks or projectiles.

Reading the Machine
During startup the collar secures the core, the arms deploy, and the segmented rings move into position and rotate. A beam feeds the top of the expanding cyan shell. Particles and branching energy make the boundary visible; stronger storm effects increase the sense of strain. Look at the machine status to confirm that protection is active and read its current radius. Outside a storm, the visible field provides the same protection and enemy damage.

During shutdown, protection contracts with the shell, the rings slow and return to alignment, and the arms fold before the core unlocks. Do not rely on the old boundary while the field is shrinking.

Saving, Moving, and Troubleshooting
The machine retains its installed core and Crystals across saving and reloading. It does not keep distant chunks loaded: an unloaded controller cannot protect an area, and incomplete loaded structures pause operation.

If placement fails, check the full footprint, solid support, liquids, and central headroom. If it will not start, finish assembly, install the correct core, and check for a manual stop during the current storm. If the radius is smaller than expected, allow startup to finish and inspect every Crystal charge level. If the core will not come out, stop the machine and wait for folding to finish.

For relocation, shut down and retrieve the contents first. Normal manual breaking of a structure part dismantles the machine and returns its controller and stored contents. Land-claim permissions still apply.

guides.h:
Temporal Triangulation and Rift Travel

The Temporal Triangulator separates rift research from portal activation so collection cannot accidentally trigger long-distance travel.

Rift Mode: Scan and Harvest
Hold Right mouse while aiming at a natural Rift from within ten blocks. Keep the beam connected for six seconds. A successful analysis collapses the Rift, deposits two measures of Residue, and records one of three triangulation locks. A Rift Harvester loaded with an empty Containment Core and placed within ten blocks captures the rift as a Rift Core. After three locks, follow the display to the convergence and stabilize the blue Convergence Rift.

A stabilized blue Convergence Rift remains safe in Rift mode. With a prepared Harvester within ten blocks, aim at it and hold Right mouse to create a Stabilized Rift Core. Harvester capture takes priority.

Collapse a Blue Rift for Residue
Without a prepared Harvester, use Rift mode to aim at the stabilized blue Convergence Rift from within ten blocks and hold Right mouse continuously for approximately six seconds. The scanner beam, moving energy, waveform, progress display, and sounds indicate the collapse. Completion closes the blue Rift and stores up to four Temporal Residue in the Triangulator. It produces no Stabilized Rift Core. The three locks clear and normal Rift searching resumes.

Releasing use, looking away, leaving range, or changing modes interrupts collapse without consuming the convergence or awarding Residue. Aim again and begin a new hold to retry. A prepared Harvester appearing nearby interrupts collapse so you can capture the Rift instead.

Travel Mode: Activate
Select Travel mode, approach the stabilized blue Convergence Rift, aim at it, and hold Right mouse to synchronize and begin random long-distance travel. Nearby players may hold use to join before departure. Travel mode never harvests or scans rifts. Random travel cannot target a chosen destination. Successful passage drains personal temporal stability and deposits four additional measures of Residue on the owner's Triangulator.

Saved Tracking Progress
Your ordered Rift locks and calculated convergence center survive logout, reconnect, server reload, and chunk unloading. Changing modes does not abandon the cycle. With fewer than three locks, continue searching for the next distinct natural Rift. The same Rift ID and Rifts within eight blocks of an existing lock cannot be locked again in that cycle. With three locks, follow the saved center guidance. An unresolved blue Rift remains available for capture, collapse, or travel after reconnecting; interrupted use actions require a fresh hold.

Capture, collapse, or successful travel completes the cycle and clears its three locks. Use /rt reset to deliberately abandon your current tracking cycle and remove its convergence.

Residue Extraction Mode
The instrument stores up to twelve measures. Extract stored Residue before collapsing a blue Rift if you want room for the full four-measure reward; any amount beyond the available capacity is not stored. Aim into open air and use this mode to recover all stored Residue.

Anchor Mode
Tracks and activates a calibrated Travel Anchor for controlled return travel. An uncharged Crystal provides one disposable return; a charged Crystal provides up to six returns and can be recharged. Read Temporal Anchor for removal and charging instructions.

Cargo Mode
Tracks Cargo Anchors, binds Cargo Transmitters, and transmits staged cargo.

Constructed Gates
A harvested Stabilized Rift Core can power a constructed Convergence Gate. Constructed gates use their own Core Housing interface and do not require a Triangulator to enter.

Safety Rule
Rift mode means scan, harvest, or deliberately collapse a blue convergence. Travel mode means enter a stabilized blue Convergence Rift. Switching modes does not remove the ready portal.

The origin of the temporal network remains unknown. Whether these pathways were created intentionally or are scars left upon reality remains a matter of debate.

Rift Recall (Optional Skill Ability)
Available through supported XSkills integrations or Prosequor, Rift Recall adds a personal orange return rift after natural blue-rift travel or exploration through a Gate powered by a natural Rift Core. Tiers unlock at Temporal Adaptation levels 10, 15, and 20, giving 10, 20, or 30 real-world minutes to return. Aim at the orange rift from within ten blocks and hold Use with the Triangulator in Travel mode until the scan finishes. The return searches for safe ground near the departure point. If no safe landing is found, the rift stays open until its deadline. A successful return closes it. A later qualifying journey replaces your previous return rift, and reconnecting does not reset its timer. Anchor returns, paired Gate travel, and Recovery Core returns do not create Rift Recall portals.
