RP Voice Chat : Starter Guide
Shout at your enemies, talk with your friends, conspire with your allies.

This mod implements VoIP to allow people on a server together to talk using microphones in-game based on proximity. It includes also a bunch of in-game communication tools !

About VoIP
To open the configuration menu you can press the keybind which by default is set to "P". Make sure to double check the keybinds. They're under user interface and have the prefix "RPVoice".
You cycle between the following speech levels with a keybind defined in your settings.

These dictate how far your voice can be heard.
●Whispering: Reaches max 5 blocks
●Talking: Reaches max 15 blocks
●Shouting: Reaches max 25 blocks

The above distances can be set per world using chat commands. Using these commands require server control privileges.
The commands are all subcommands of "/rpvc" so just use "/help rpvc" and you should get more information.

Communication tools
RP Voice Chat includes more than VoIP. You will find items and blocks that will give you new ways to communicate. For example :
●Horns
●Bells
●Megaphones
●Lights
●Telegraph
●Telephone
●Radio

RP Voice Chat : Horns

Horns are wind instruments used to communicate orders or alerts from a distance. Each has its use:

●Royal horn: forged musical instrument, to harangue the people
●Warhorn: horn whose sound resounds over long distances to warn its allies

RP Voice Chat : Bells

Bells have always announced victories, defeats, festivities or deaths. You will find a bell for each use:

●Handbell: short-range hand bell
●Callbell: counter bell to alert of its presence
●Small bell parts: element used for the first two items but usable on doors
●Carillon bell: bell emitting a different tone depending on the metal used
●Church bell: bell so big that it has to be welded
●Bell hammer: powered by mechanical power, strikes carillon or church bells

RP Voice Chat : Telegraph

The telegraph system allows transmitting coded messages over long distances through a network of wires and specialized equipment. This revolutionary technology enables you to communicate silently with your allies over great distances, perfect for coordinating strategies or transmitting sensitive information.

The telegraph works through an audible sound code within a limited radius around the device.

●Telegraph key: main device for sending and receiving coded messages
●Telegraph wire: spool allowing connection of equipment
●Insulator: essential connector for extending and structuring your telegraph network
●Wire cutter: tool for cutting wire connections to reconfigure networks
●Printer: prints telegrams when placed under a telegraph key; requires paper slips
●Switchboard: orchestrates network typing and unlocks advanced addressing when powered

Setup
How to wire telegraph networks

RP Voice Chat : Megaphones

Megaphones amplify your voice far beyond normal speech range. You will be able to use different models:

●Megaphone: carries your voice up to 125 blocks; still affected by distance and obstacles
●Administrator's Megaphone: exceptional device, whose manufacturing secret Jonas took to his grave, carrying voice over long distances and through matter

RP Voice Chat : Lights

After illumination, we soon found another use for light: to communicate. You will find a light source for each use:

●Signal lamp: lamp that lights up when you hold Right mouse, for signaling and communication

RP Voice Chat : Telephone

The wired telephone system brings your settlement into the era of modern communication. From a simple local line to an organized network, it lets you transmit voice over distance between connected endpoints. You can use it in direct mode (two telephones), in broadcast mode (one telephone to one or more speakers), or in a managed network with dialing.

●Telephone: voice endpoint for calling, answering, and talking
●Speaker: audio output linked to a telephone for voice broadcast
●Telegraph wire: cable used to connect network elements
●Insulator: connection support used to extend the wired network
●Wire cutter: maintenance tool used to remove connections
●Switchboard: network manager for advanced routing, dialing, and capacity

Setup
How to wire telephone networks

RP Voice Chat : Radio

Where the cable ends, the ether continues. Build a radio station for live or streamed programs, raise an antenna, and let receivers hear you across the Seraph lands — or run a small speaker broadcast off a tuned radio set.

●Station console: sets frequency and station name
●Radio transmitter: RF broadcast when powered; stack antenna segments for range
●Antenna segment: extends transmitter range; cover mid-stack like wall axles
●Radio microphone: live voice into the station bus
●Mixing console: HLS program feed and mic mix when on-air
●Radio receiver: tunes stations locally; one wire + up to 4 speakers for local broadcast
●Talkie: portable RF transceiver
●Speaker: wired speaker output for telephone or radio-receiver branches
●Telegraph wire: station cabling and receiver speaker branches
Setup
How to build radio setups

Telegraph networks

Wire the network with telegraph wire (max 20 blocks between two points). Use insulators to extend the line further. In both configurations below, place a printer under a key with paper slips to keep telegrams.

1) Open line (no switchboard)
Wire telegraph keys together through insulators as needed. There is no power requirement and no hard key limit, but each key accepts only one wire. Messages are heard as sound near the key (short range) and clear after a few seconds.

2) Managed network (switchboard)
Add a powered switchboard (default: at least 10% mechanical power, up to 8 keys; more switchboards on the same managed network stack capacity). You can then name the keys and choose where each message is sent.

Telephone networks

Cable everything with telegraph wire and insulators when you need longer runs. Only one network topology is allowed. Trying to mix them will deny the wire connection.

1) Local line
Wire two telephones directly (insulators allowed). No switchboard. Right mouse-click a telephone to call the other one.

2) Broadcast line
Wire one telephone to up to eight speakers (insulators allowed). Only one telephone may sit on a speaker branch. Speakers play the caller's voice along the line.

3) Managed network (switchboard)
Connect several telephones to a powered switchboard (default: at least 25% power, up to 16 phones; capacity stacks with more switchboards). Assign numbers and dial between endpoints. Speakers cannot join a switchboard-managed network.

Radio setups

Do not mix network types on the same wires: a radio station, a speaker line off a receiver, and a telephone or telegraph network must each stay as their own separate installation.

1) Transmit station
Wire one station console to a transmitter (optional: microphone and/or mixing console). Only one console per station. Power the transmitter (default: at least 50% mechanical power), set frequency and name on the console, then stack antenna segments on the transmitter for range.

2) Listen over RF
Place a radio receiver, tune the station frequency, set local playback range, and turn it on. Or carry a talkie tuned to the same frequency within antenna (or talkie) range.

3) Receiver speaker branch
From a receiver, run a single wire to up to four speakers (insulators allowed). That branch may only contain the receiver, connectors, and speakers.

4) Repeater (optional)
Set a powered transmitter to repeater mode and choose the frequency to relay. In repeater mode, existing wires stay in place but go dormant for the station; you cannot add new ones. Switch back to wired-source mode to reactivate the console, microphone, and mixing console.

The primary source of information is the mod's guidebook Manual of Magical Arts. The secondary source of information are survival handbook entries for individual items/blocks.

To get started, look for rifts in the world. Any flowers around them will have a chance to be converted temporarily into Unstable riftblooms. Harvest these with a knife for a chance to get a riftbloom seed. Plant that seed in the ground and let it grow. This can be planted anywhere flowers can be placed. Once it is mature, harvest with a knife to get rusty dust and shifting fibers. Use the rusty dust to unlock magic. All info and more can be found in the Manual of Magical Arts.

Shipwright Constructions

Constructing any boat starts with a construction site. These construction items have all the needed resources for their respective boat listed in the handbook. Once crafted, select it in your hotbar and an in-world schematic will appear. You can change the direction the schematic faces using the F key. Place it on a flat area (making sure the blue highlighted schematic strip is in water).

Afterwards, if you have block interaction help turned on (toggle with blockinteractionhelp), looking at the in-process boat will show you the next required ingredients.

Any boat using linen sails can be recolored with a sail-recolor item.

Only the smallest boats can be picked up again, all others can only be dismantled.
Deconstruction: You can deconstruct any boat to get a portion of the materials back by rightmouse it with a saw. You will have to hold the mouse button down for some time, before this will be completed.

Hitbox = slot.

Chisel voxel pillars using different materials for each hitbox. The game optimizes voxels horizontally, and using voxel pillars is the only way to prevent this optimization.
For example, if you want hitboxes arranged in a checkerboard pattern, you only need two different materials.

Step 1 - Get a head
Harvest a carcass with a knife as usual. Along with the meat and hide there is sometimes the animal's head - how often depends on the server's settings. Most animals also give their own pelt, cut from their coat.

Step 2 - Preserve the head
Seal the raw head in a barrel with 1 litre of diluted borax for 18 hours, or 1 litre of zinc sulfate for 12 hours.

Or skin it instead
A raw head can be skinned rather than preserved. Place it on the ground and hold right-click on it with a knife: the head is used up, and what you manage to cut from it - the hide, meat, fat and bones - drops on the ground. A slip of the knife can ruin any of them. Antlers, horns and tusks come off whole.

Step 3 - Prepare the pelt
A mount is stuffed with a pelt of the same animal - a whitetail's head takes a whitetail pelt. Foxes, raccoons and bears take the game's own pelt of their kind. If the server has own pelts switched off, any plain pelt of the right size will do. To make the pelt, put the animal's raw hide in the crafting grid with rendered fat to oil it, the same as any hide; the oiled hide cures into a pelt after 48 hours. The preserved head's tooltip names the pelt it needs.

Step 4 - Make the mount
You need its pelt (with own pelts switched off on the server, a plain pelt of the same size - the head's tooltip says which), dry grass - 2 for a small pelt, 4 medium, 6 large, 8 huge - and a needle and thread. Two ways to put them together:
• In the crafting grid: the preserved head, the pelt, the grass and the needle and thread. It uses as many stitches as the grass.
• In the world: put the preserved head on the ground and right-click it with the pelt, then right-click with dry grass until it has enough. Hold right-click with the needle and thread to sew it into the finished mount - it uses as many stitches as the grass. Until it is sewn, breaking it gives every part back.

Needle and thread
In the crafting grid, a knife, a bone and flax twine make a threaded needle in one go (a knife and a bone alone make the game's flute). On the ground: put a bone down and hold right-click on it with a knife (sneak + knife still carves the flute), then put the bare needle down and hold right-click on it with flax twine. It holds 60 stitches; when the thread runs out you get the bare needle back - thread it again with flax twine, in the grid or on the ground.

Step 5 - Place and pose it
Right-click a block to place the mount; it faces you. With an empty hand, sneak + right-click it to open its window: choose a pose, then move, turn and tilt it. Right-click with an empty hand to pick it up again - everything is remembered. There is no base: the mount stands on whatever block is beneath it, slabs and chiselled blocks included.

Heads on the wall
Put one of the game's antler mounts on a wall and right-click it with a preserved head. With an empty hand, sneak + right-click to adjust the head, or right-click to take it down.

The BASICs is primarily an RP chat and character identity mod. It adds proximity roleplay chat, visible character sheets, nicknames, notes, teleport requests, player stats, and staff tools. Server config controls which features are enabled, what privileges they require, ranges, formatting, and whether helper systems such as chatter, bubbles, languages, notes, TPA, or stats are available.

Start here
- Use /thebasics help for the short command summary.
- Use /thebasics guide or press H and choose The BASICs in the handbook.
- Use /say, /whisper, /yell, /me, /it, and /ooc for RP chat.
- Use /nick and /nickcolor for RP display names when enabled.
- Use Ctrl+Shift+B or /charsheet to open your character sheet when character sheets are enabled.
- Use /chatprefs help if roleplay colors are hard to read.
- Use /notes for private notes and /adminnotes <player> for staff notes when you have permission.

Guide pages
- RP Chat: proximity speech, emotes, OOC, nicknames, bubbles, and chatter.
- Character Sheets: bios, /look, headshots, character slots, and nickname integration.
- Languages and Accessibility: language prefixes, language colors, and chat color presets.
- Notes: private notes, staff notes, structured entries, and freeform ledgers.
- TPA: request-based teleporting and optional temporal gear costs.
- Player Stats: tracked deaths, kills, block breaks, travel, and staff cleanup.
- Utilities: save notifications, sleep notices, and repair helper tools.
- Staff and Config: admin config, chat inspection, command help, and permissions.

RP chat is the core of The BASICs. When enabled, normal chat becomes proximity-based roleplay text with configurable ranges, formatting, overhead bubbles, OOC behavior, and chatter sounds. Server config can turn the RP pipeline on or off, change ranges, require nicknames or character sheet fields, enable or disable shortcuts, and gate commands by privilege.

Speech modes
- /say [message], aliases /s and /normal: speak normally or set your default mode to normal.
- /whisper [message], alias /w: whisper once or set whisper as your default mode.
- /yell [message], alias /y: yell once or set yell as your default mode.
Server config can tune each mode's range or disable the mode.

Emotes and environment text
- /me <emote>: proximity emote.
- /it <message> or /do <message>: nearby environmental description.
- /envhere <message>: place environment text where you are looking; if no surface is hit, it falls back above you.
- /emotemode [on|off]: make ordinary proximity messages act like emotes unless another syntax says otherwise.

Nicknames
Nicknames are part of RP chat and predate character sheets.
- /nick [name]: view or set your RP display name when enabled.
- /clearnick: clear your nickname.
- /nickcolor [color] and /clearnickcolor: manage nickname color when enabled.
If character sheets are also enabled, nickname commands can update the configured nickname sheet field, so nicknames also appear in the Character Sheets page.

Typing shortcuts
Server config controls these shortcuts. Defaults may include *text for emote, !text for environment, !!text for placed environment text, //text for OOC, (text) for low/OOC, and ((text)) for global OOC.

Visual and audio helpers
- Overhead chat bubbles, typing indicators, and chatter sounds are config toggles.
- /chatprefs opens color preferences; /chatprefs help lists commands.
- /chatprefs preset <highcontrast|classic|default> can quickly improve readability.

Character sheets are the shiny identity layer for RP: visible bios, /look details, configurable fields, headshots, and optional character slots. Server owners can enable or disable the system, choose fields, require values before RP chat, control visibility, and decide which fields appear in /look.

Player commands
- /charsheet or /sheet: open your editable sheet.
- /charsheet <player>: view another online player's visible sheet fields.
- /bio: quick view alias for character sheets.
- /look or /look <player>: inspect a nearby player. Without a name, it uses the player you are targeting.
- /charsheetfields: list configured sheet fields and visibility.
- /setcharsheet <field> <value>: set a field from chat. Aliases include /setsheet and /setbio.
- /clearcharsheet [field]: clear one field, or all editable fields when no field is given. Aliases include /clearsheet and /clearbio.

/look rules
/look is meant for in-character inspection. By default the target must be online, nearby, and in line of sight, but range and line-of-sight rules are configurable. Self-look opens your full editable sheet. Fields marked self-only or admin-only are hidden from other players.

Nicknames and display names
Nicknames belong to RP chat, but character sheets can integrate with them. When the configured nickname field exists, /nick and /nickcolor can update sheet-backed display information. The default display priority is Full Name (Nickname), then Full Name, then Nickname, then account name.

Headshots
When enabled, your editable sheet can accept a PNG/JPEG drop for a character portrait. Server config controls size limits and whether direct image URLs are allowed. /clearheadshot removes your portrait.

Character slots
If RP character slots are enabled, use /character or /characters to list slots, inspect the active slot, create/switch/delete slots, and manage per-character data. Slot limits and deletion rules are server-configurable.

Languages can mark speech as Common, Tradeband, Sign, or server-defined languages. This system only appears when enabled by server config.

Player language commands
- /addlang <language>: learn a language when allowed.
- /removelang <language>: remove a language when allowed.
- /listlang: list your known, learning, and unknown languages.

Speaking a language
Use a prefix before your message, such as :c hello for Common or :tr hello for Tradeband. Using only the prefix, such as :c, changes your default speaking language. Unknown or unlearned languages are rejected. Sign language has its own range rules and may require line of sight.

Learning comprehension
Staff can set partial comprehension for a language. A 40% comprehension level means roughly 40% of the words in that language remain readable for that player while the rest stay scrambled. Fully known languages are always understood at 100%.

Chat accessibility
Use /chatprefs or /chatprefs status to view your current settings. Use /chatprefs help for syntax. Common options include language colors, labels, nickname colors, and color presets.

Useful accessibility commands
- /chatprefs preset highcontrast
- /chatprefs preset coloruniversal
- /chatprefs preset protanopia
- /chatprefs preset deuteranopia
- /chatprefs preset tritanopia
- /chatprefs preset monochrome
- /langcolor [on|off]: shortcut for language color display.

If a color or label makes chat harder to read, change it locally. These preferences affect your chat view; they do not change what other players see.

Notes provide server-side writing tools for roleplay, memory, and staff coordination. Notes open a GUI with an entry list, a selected entry editor, a freeform notes area, and Reload, Save, Close, and Guide buttons. Closing or reloading with unsaved changes asks for confirmation.

Private notes
Private notes are visible only to you. Use them for personal reminders, character details, or private observations about another player.

Commands:
- /notes: open your private notes about yourself.
- /notes about <player>: open your private notes about another known player.
- /notes help: show syntax.
- /notes list, /notes add <text>, /notes view <id>, /notes edit <id> <text>, /notes delete <id> confirm.
Aliases include /personalnotes and /pnotes.

Staff notes
Staff notes are shared staff-only notes about a player account. They require the configured admin notes privilege. Staff notes can include structured timestamped entries and, when enabled, a freeform staff ledger.

Commands:
- /adminnotes <player>: open staff notes for a player.
- /adminnotes help: show syntax.
- /adminnotes <player> list, add <text>, view <id>, edit <id> <text>, delete <id> confirm.
- /adminnotes <player> ledger view and /adminnotes <player> ledger set <text>.
Aliases include /anotes and /staffnotes.

Caveats
Player lookup can find offline players known to the server. Note IDs can be abbreviated only when the prefix uniquely matches. Delete commands require confirm. Staff note changes are audit-logged.

TPA is request-based teleporting. The target player must accept before anyone teleports. Server config controls whether TPA is enabled, what privilege is required, request timeout, request cooldowns, accepted-teleport warmups, and whether sending a request consumes a temporal gear.

TPA commands
- /tpa <player>: ask to teleport to another player.
- /tpahere <player>: ask another player to teleport to you.
- /tpaccept [player]: accept an incoming request. The player name is optional when only one request exists.
- /tpdeny [player]: deny an incoming request.
- /tpalist: list incoming requests and remaining time when timeouts are enabled.
- /tpallow on|off: allow or block receiving requests.
- /tpacancel: cancel your outgoing request.
- /cleartpa: clear all incoming requests to you.

Warmups
If TPA warmups are enabled, accepting a request starts a stand-still wait before the teleport completes. For /tpa, the requester must stand still after the target accepts. For /tpahere, the accepting target must stand still before being brought to the requester. Moving, taking damage, or interacting can cancel the accepted teleport.

Temporal gear behavior
When the temporal gear requirement is enabled, the requester must hold a temporal gear in either hand. The gear is consumed after the request passes validation. If the request is denied, cleared, cancelled, times out, or the accepted warmup is cancelled, the gear is returned to inventory, hand, or dropped at the requester's feet if there is no room.

Player stats are optional server-side counters. Server config controls whether the stats system is enabled and which counters are tracked.

Player command
- /playerstats [player] or /pstats [player]: view your stats or another online player's stats when enabled.

Tracked stats
Stats can include deaths, player kills, NPC kills, blocks broken, and distance travelled. Each counter can be enabled or disabled by server config.

Staff cleanup
- /clearstats <player> confirm: clear all stats for an online player.
- /clearstat <player> <stat> confirm: clear one stat. Valid stat names include DEATHS, KILLS_PLAYER, KILLS_NPC, BLOCK_BREAKS, and DISTANCE_TRAVELLED.
The clear commands require the configured player-stat clear privilege.

Teleportation collects The BASICs' non-request teleport tools. All five command families default to opt-in when their settings are absent; existing explicitly saved true or false values remain in effect. Enable the desired Teleportation.Register... settings, then restart the server so The BASICs can register those commands. Server config also controls privileges, warmups, cooldowns, temporal gear costs, and safety gates. Staff can inspect and adjust live settings with /thebasics config; most non-registration teleport settings are live reloadable.

Homes
- /sethome: save your default home.
- /sethome <name>: save a named home.
- /home: return to your default home.
- /home <name>: return to a named home.
- /homes: list saved homes.
- /delhome <name>: delete a saved home. Use /delhome default for your default home.

Spawn
- /spawn: teleport to The BASICs spawn, or to the world's default spawn if staff have not set one.
- /setspawn: staff command that sets The BASICs spawn destination without changing vanilla respawn behavior.

Back
- /back: return to the spot recorded before your last server-side teleport. It stores one previous location and expires after the configured window. A successful /back records the place you left, so repeated /back uses can move between the two latest teleport locations after any configured cooldown. This first pass only supports same-dimension return locations. The global recorder runs only when Teleportation.RegisterBackCommand is enabled, and catches The BASICs teleports, accepted TPA teleports, and vanilla teleports that go through the normal player teleport path.

Top and stuck
- /top: teleport to a safe surface above your current vertical column, checking adjacent columns if needed. Teleportation.TopRequireTemporalGear can add a live-reloadable temporal gear cost; it defaults off.
- /stuck: slow, gear-free emergency teleport to spawn. It can remind the waiting player, notify staff, and optionally refuse to run while another online player has the configured help/admin privilege. Set that block privilege empty to always allow /stuck.

Warmups and cancellation
When warmups are enabled, stand still until the teleport completes. Moving, taking damage, or interacting can cancel the warmup depending on config. Cooldowns start after a successful teleport. Temporal gear requirements are checked before warmup and consumed only when the teleport completes; failed safety searches and cancelled warmups do not consume a gear.

Enabling commands
Enable only the desired Teleportation.RegisterHomeCommands, RegisterSpawnCommands, RegisterStuckCommand, RegisterTopCommand, and RegisterBackCommand settings, then restart. Player-facing command privileges remain configurable and default to chat after opt-in; /setspawn remains restricted to commandplayer by default.

Utilities is the small-tools drawer for The BASICs. These features are not the main RP experience, but they help server operations and quality of life. Server config controls the notification-style features, and root privileges gate repair tools.

Home and spawn
Players can use /sethome to save their default home and /home to return to it. Named homes use /sethome <name>, /home <name>, /homes, and /delhome <name>; server config controls how many homes each player can save. Players can use /spawn to return to the server spawn. Staff can use /setspawn to set The BASICs' spawn destination; until that is set, /spawn uses the world's default spawn. Server config can add warmups, cooldowns, and an optional temporal gear cost for /home and /spawn. When warmups are enabled, stand still until the teleport completes; moving, taking damage, or interacting can cancel it.

Top and stuck recovery
Players can use /top to move to a safe surface above their current vertical column, checking adjacent columns if needed. It is intended for vertical escape and has its own warmup, cooldown, privilege, and optional temporal gear cost. Teleportation.TopRequireTemporalGear defaults off and can be changed live; gear is consumed only if the teleport completes. Players can use /stuck as a much slower, gear-free emergency teleport to spawn when something is genuinely wrong and staff are unavailable. It has its own long warmup, reminders, cooldown, staff notifications, and an optional setting that blocks use while another online player has the configured admin/help privilege.

Save notifications
When enabled by config, the server can announce when a save starts and when it finishes. The announcement can be sent as chat text or as a client notification depending on config. Expect brief lag during saves.

Sleep notifier
The sleep notifier system can help servers communicate sleep state. Its exact behavior depends on server config and the active Vintage Story sleep rules.

Repair helper
The root-gated /setdurability <durability> command changes the held durable item's current durability. Use a raw durability number or /setdurability 100% to fully repair it. This is an administrative utility, not a normal player repair system.

guides.t: The BASICs: Staff and Server Tools
guides.h:
Staff and server tools are permission-gated. Most staff commands require the configured staff privilege, and server config commands require root.

Staff notes
- /adminnotes <player>, aliases /anotes and /staffnotes: open shared staff-only notes.
- Structured staff commands: list, add, view, edit, delete <id> confirm.
- Freeform staff ledger: /adminnotes <player> ledger view and ledger set <text>.

Character sheet staff commands
- /adminviewcharsheet <player>: view all fields, including admin-only fields. Aliases include /adminviewsheet and /adminviewbio.
- /adminsetcharsheet <player> <field> <value>: set a field. Aliases include /adminsetsheet and /adminsetbio.
- /adminclearcharsheet <player> [field]: clear one field or all editable fields.
- /adminclearheadshot <player>: clear another player's headshot.

Identity and language staff commands
- /adminsetnick <player> <nickname>: set an RP chat nickname. Use force before the nickname to bypass conflict warnings.
- /adminsetnickcolor <player> <color>: set nickname color.
- /adminaddlang, /adminremovelang, and /adminlistlang: manage player languages when the language system is enabled.

Stats and server config
- /clearstats and /clearstat: clear player stats when you have the configured player-stat clear privilege.
- /thebasics config: open the config admin panel.
- /thebasics config languages: edit language definitions.
- /thebasics config charsheetfields: edit character sheet fields.
- /thebasics reloadconfig: reload config from disk.
The config panel marks changed settings that need restart separately from settings that apply live.

Your first steps in Vintage Canvas

Welcome to Vintage Canvas! To begin your creative journey, you'll need a couple of things at minimum: an easel, any shape of canvas, and a charcoal stick.

Place your easel in the world (ideally somewhere with good light). Place your canvas onto the easel using Right mouse. Then, hold your charcoal stick, and sketch away to your heart's content!

To show off your creation, take it out of the easel with an empty hand, and put it up on any wall. For some extra flair, you can use any wooden board to frame the canvas while it's hanging up!

Blending
If your sketch is looking too coarse for your liking, consider crafting a brush. A brush without any paint serves as a blender, letting you create smooth gradients and lighter colours. To correct mistakes, consider making a chalk stick.

Painting
Once you're ready for a bigger challenge, it's time to create some paint! Make a couple of paint jars, fill them with some oil, and add any pigment - like crushed lapis lazuli, cinnabar, charcoal - or one of the new pigments added by Vintage Canvas. If you’re short on oil, you can create an alternate medium called ‘tempera’ by adding an egg to a paint jar full of water.

Next, craft yourself one or all of the paint brushes. Right-click to dip your paint in the jar of your choice, and paint away!

If you're looking for more than the flat colours of basic pigments, you have two options: paint thinning, and paint mixing.

Paint Thinning
To reduce the opacity of your paint, dip your brush with paint into a jar of turpentine. The more times you dip it, the more transparent the paint - ideal for making blended colours!

Paint mixing
Still not satisfied with the colours at your disposal? Time to craft a palette! When placed in the world, this nifty plank gives you nine slots in which to combine basic paints. Click any slot with a paint jar to add its colour to the mix. Keep adding paints until you've got your ideal tone! Right-click the slot with a brush to use the paint, same as any paint jar. To clean out a slot, right-click it with your turpentine jar.

Blending
You can use a fresh, paintless brush to blend colours on the canvas. To clean out a brush, crouch + right-click your brush onto a turpentine jar.

The simplest way to paint

As an alternative to canvases, Vintage Canvas also supports fresco painting. To make a fresco, craft some fresco plaster or primer. Apply this to a chiselled block (non-chiselled blocks are not currently supported), and use any of your painting tools to display your talents directly on the walls. Use white plaster for a canvas-like backdrop, or transparent primer to keep the original block visible.

To erase parts of the texture, use a turpentine rag.

Note that frescos are fragile, and can’t be picked up without being destroyed. To make portable art, you’ll need to use a canvas.

Large paintings
To paint a large canvas, you need a large easel. Once you've got one set up, you can combine any two canvases into their corresponding upgraded size. You get four times the surface area for just twice the materials, so it's an excellent deal!

Frames
You can add frames to your canvases by placing them in the world, and right-clicking them while holding a wooden board. Click again to cycle between styles or to remove the frame.

Naming and signing
To claim permanent authorship over your painting, you can right-click your easel with an Ink and Quill. This lets you name your painting and sign your name to it, which nobody else will be able to change!

By default, paint slowly gets consumed as you use brushes, palettes, and jars. If you just want to paint without interruption, you can toggle this setting off in the mod config (PaintDepletion: false). Alternatively, you can increase the amount of painting you can do with a given amount of paint.

guides.t: Mod Mechanic: Building a Tier 1 Air-Raft
guides.h:
Air-Raft Construction

Constructing a Tier 1 air-raft requires a great deal of materials and many steps, but it all starts with a Tier 1 air-raft yard kit (14x7).

Once you've transcribed enough airship research for crafting the aerostatica, use it to craft an air-raft schematic (Tier 1). Use this schematic to craft the shipyard kit.

If you hold the shipyard kit in your hotbar, an in-world schematic box of 7 blocks wide by 14 blocks long will appear in front of you. Place the yard kit on a flat area and make sure to face the shipyard in the direction you want the air-raft to launch in. You can change the direction the shipyard faces by using the [F] key. Once placed down, you will be standing by the front side of the yard.

Afterwards, if you have block interaction help turned on (toggle with blockinteractionhelp), looking at the shipyard lectern will show you the next steps. You will need logs and boards of the same wood type.

For a Tier 1 air-raft's balloon, you will need to gather enough flax twine to produce a visually calculated total of 100 units of plain cloth. Make sure to prepare a flax farm greenhouse with the right fertilizer!

(We have also made a standalone mod which adds multiplied crafting outputs in windmill driven crafting machines to help with this high demand of cloth. This mod is called Clothier's Heirlooms.)

All plain cloth will need to be treated with balloon coating liquid.

The mod config will allow you to set the amount of balloon coating liquid consumed per sealing, which allows you to change the eventual total amount of required items needed to craft enough balloon coating mixture for the coating process. For more information and detailed explanation about this, please visit the modDB page description and look for COATING LIQUID GRIND CONFIGURATION. Thank you!

See the Tier 1 air-raft for more information on how to equip your new air-raft.

You can carry the air-raft like a backpack by holding Shift and clicking Right mouse on it. (You will not be able to pack it up if it has attachments.)

As a backpack, it can be unpacked and deployed by holding Ctrl and scrolling to the backpack slot, then clicking Right mouse to place it on the ground.

The air-raft can also be placed as ground storage. Hold Shift and click Right mouse to place it on the ground.

It can be scrapped for a partial return of materials by holding Right mouse with a saw in your hand.

guides.h:

Place the yard kit on a flat area and make sure to face the shipyard in the direction you want the air-boat to launch in. You can change the direction the shipyard faces by using the F key. Once placed down, you will be standing by the right side of the yard.

Afterwards, if you have block interaction help turned on (toggle with blockinteractionhelp), looking at the shipyard lectern will show you the next steps.

You will need logs and boards of the same wood type. For a Tier 2 air-boat's balloon, you will need to gather enough flax twine to produce a visually calculated total of 224 units of plain cloth.

Make sure to prepare a flax farm greenhouse with the right fertilizer!

(We have made a standalone mod which adds multiplied crafting outputs in windmill driven crafting machines to help with this high demand of cloth. This mod is called Clothier's Heirlooms.)

All cloth will need to be treated with balloon coating liquid. The mod config will allow you to set the amount of balloon coating liquid consumed per sealing, which allows you to change the eventual total amount of required items needed to craft enough balloon coating mixture for the coating process.

For more information and detailed explanation about this, please visit the modDB page description and look for COATING LIQUID GRIND CONFIGURATION. Thank you!

See the Tier 2 air-boat for more information on how to equip your new air-boat.

Skills

Skill
A skill is a collection of your knowledge and your abilities in a specific field. Each of your skills has a specific level. You can increase this level by gathering experience doing activities related to this skill. With every level you also receive an ability point for this skill. To see an overview of your skills and abilities press the [O] key(default). You can change this key in the settings menu.

Ability
An ability gives you a specific advantage for a specific skill related activity. Most abilities have more than one tiers. Higher tiers of an ability provide more advantages. To increase the tier of an ability you need one ability point of the skill the ability belongs to. Than you can click on the ability in the skill dialog to increase its tier. You can also decrease the tier of an ability. To do so you must toggle the mode to unlearn mode by clicking the unlearn button. Now you can click on the ability to decrease the tier of the ability. Remember to toggle the unlearn button again to disable the unlearn mode. Notice that you need unlearn points to decrease the tier of an ability. When you decrease the tier of an ability you will get back the ability point you used. While ability points are bound to a specific skill, unlearn points are shared across all skills. You can receive unlearn points from consuming specific items. These items can be found in the handbook.

Sparring
If two players have sparring mode enabled and kill each other, neither of them will loose experience points upon dying.
